about: Truth was written by the assistant, one labeller, not a licensed examiner. Generated sets and planted erasures carry their truth from how they were made. Real sets were audited sheet by sheet by two auditors working blind to Storey, and one adjudicator ruled on each item. Richmond is the exception: its truth is the examiner's letter on its one sheet, not an audit, so it is scored on which of the letter's 10 sheet-only comments were raised, and no finding there is judged false. A wrong pass is a stair shown Found where truth says it is absent or was erased, or a comment shown Looks resolved where truth holds it open. Storey shows no pass for any other check, so a defect it does not raise is a miss, listed by name. On army_bt_bcof and queens_royce, stair truth gives each stair's place on every floor, drawn or absent. Their wrong passes are counted over the cells where truth says a stair is absent, and on their planted copies over the erased cells too, and the cells where truth says a stair is drawn are counted by the state Storey showed. A stair that ends at a floor is no defect, so an absent cell is never a miss. A stair row Storey shows where truth places no stair on any floor, drawn or absent, is counted apart: each Found cell there is listed as found where truth places no stair, not as a wrong pass, because truth leaves out some stair-like marks on purpose, such as the walk-off grilles on army_bt_bcof. queens_royce has stair truth alone, so no finding there is judged. Findings judged real count Fix and Check items. Cannot tell items are not claims and are counted apart. On generated sets, a finding with no planted cause counts as false. On planted erasures, truth covers stair presence alone, so for both methods a finding that names no erased stair is counted as not judged. A second review is also scored on a change planted with no cloud round it, which only a comparison with the first set can show, so the baseline, shown one set, is not scored on that change. The baseline is Meta's muse-spark-1.3 asked once per set, every sheet in one request, with a plain prompt that names none of Storey's checks. It shows no stair matrix and no comment states, so it has no wrong passes to count. Cost and minutes come only from a run eval.run began in a new folder on a cold model cache, and are blank otherwise. A second review shares its first review's cache, as it would on the server. Each number carries its status. Development numbers come from sets that earlier experiments touched. Held-out numbers come only from army_bt_bcof, queens_royce and their planted copies, from each one's one run on code, scoring and truth frozen by hash. A run with no truth hash recorded, or whose truth changed after it, is post hoc. On mml_capitol, findings from rules written after its audit are counted apart as post hoc. That split goes by rule, so a later change to how an older rule reads the drawing stays in the development row.
